> Although this would require some spec changes to define these objects and make sure the targets are correct in any specs that reference them.

Actually looking at some prior art in the html spec, workers already use implied [retargeting of their events on the hidden messageport to the worker itself](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/workers.html#dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface):

> All messages received by that port must immediately be retargeted at the [DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/workers.html#dedicatedworkerglobalscope) object.

Similar language could be used if we had a `globalThis.events` or something like so:

> All events received on a global object must be retargeted to the global object's _effective event target_.

Where we define for `Window`/`WorkerGlobalScope`/etc that their _effective event target_ is just the object themselves, but for shadow realms `HostInitializeShadowRealm` would set the _effective event target_ to `globalThis.events`.

I share @domenic 's intuition that we would initially fire these events (both unhandled exceptions and rejections) at the principle Realm. I wouldn't be so opposed to making the ShadowRealm global object an EventTarget just for this purpose, though; that's one way of configuring this, but there are other options, which could be pursued after initially shipping this feature (e.g., an options bag passed to the ShadowRealm constructor); we're forward-compatible as long as we assume that, if a handler isn't registered, the exception/rejection is forwarded to the principal Realm.

What might be missing in the current specification is ensuring that the principal Realm exception is sent there, rather than the original value. In https://github.com/tc39/proposal-shadowrealm/issues/353#issuecomment-1176571443 , there's discussion of ways to make some of the information from the original exception visible, while still using the appropriate Realm; the conclusion of that discussion should somehow be applied here.
